messages.content: Write a polished short scene in modern American English between two adult friends using humor while one is quietly having a rough day. The humor should arise from familiarity rather than constant punchlines. Let one sincere moment land without turning the scene sentimental. Keep the dialogue and actions natural.

“You look terrible.”

Riley dropped onto the couch. “Thanks.”

“I mean emotionally.”

“That somehow made it worse.”

Sam handed her a bowl.

Riley looked inside. “What is this?”

“Soup.”

“Why is it green?”

“Vegetables.”

“I don't trust green soup.”

“You don't have to trust it. You have to eat it.”

Riley picked up the spoon and took a cautious bite.

She waited.

“Well?” Sam asked.

“I've had worse.”

“That is the highest compliment you've ever given me.”

“Don't let it change you.”

Sam smiled and sat back.

Riley ate another spoonful.

After a minute, she said, “I got bad news today.”

Sam's smile faded.

“I figured.”

Riley looked at her.

“You've been making jokes for ten minutes,” Sam said. “You only do that when you don't want to talk.”

Riley stared into the bowl.

“I'm not ready.”

“Okay.”

Sam reached for the remote.

“Pick something stupid.”

Riley looked over. “That's your plan?”

“It's one of my better plans.”

“You have terrible plans.”

“I know.”

A small smile appeared on Riley's face.

“Put on the cooking show.”

“The one where they yell at each other?”

“That's the one.”

Sam turned it on.

Riley took another bite of soup.

“This is still terrible.”

“You're still eating it.”

“I'm grieving.”

“Dramatic.”

“Accurate.”

Sam smiled again, quieter this time.

“Yeah.”
